findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — Ruby has no overloading: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at :149 silently replaces `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at :145, so the advertised width/height variant is dead code and any caller using the pre-existing 5-positional contract `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4) while a 4-positional caller binds `h` as `opts`; the model now exposes two incompatible contracts under one name with only the last one live. (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` mutates the file by path while the loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` read through Rack's still-open fd; `convert_with` finishes with `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` which replaces the path via rename (new inode), after which `Tempfile#size` (fstat on the old unlinked inode; verified: rename leaves `t.size`=stale, `File.size(t.path)`=new) is frozen at the pre-optimisation size, so the `while tempfile.size > max` guard keeps shrinking an already-compliant file for all 5 attempts and the persisted `filesize` describes bytes that were never stored. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 + app/models/optimized_image.rb:155 — animated-GIF dispatch is keyed on the *temp path* (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) but browser uploads arrive as Rack multipart tempfiles named `Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")` with no extension, so `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` can never select the gifsicle path and every oversized animated GIF is flattened to its first frame by `convert path[0]`; the format decision belongs to the caller that owns `filename`, not to a regex over a tempfile name. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the new pre-upload downsize gates on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` (which includes svg) but omits the SVG exemption that the same model's `OptimizedImage.create_for` applies at optimized_image.rb:45-47, so an SVG over `max_image_size_kb` is fed to `convert ... -resize 80%` and rewritten as a rasterised ImageMagick "SVG"; the two entry points into the resizer now disagree on which formats are resizable. (P2, conf 50)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hard-coded `10 * 1024` breaks the client contract for *attachments* too: the server still enforces `max_attachment_size_kb`/`max_image_size_kb` (uploads_controller.rb:64-66 still reads the setting) so a 5 MB attachment against a 3 MB limit now passes the pre-flight, is fully uploaded, and is rejected server-side; admins can no longer raise the client limit above 10 MB or lower it at all. (P2, conf 100)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 + app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — "10 MB" exists as three unrelated literals with three different meanings (client pre-flight cap, client-side text for a 413 that is actually produced by nginx `client_max_body_size`, and the server cap that applies only to API URL downloads at :55, not to multipart uploads), with no shared constant or site setting; the 413 alert asserts a 10 MB limit the server never enforces and nginx may set anywhere. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-69 — the loop discards `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s boolean and has no outcome channel: after 5 failed or insufficient attempts control falls straight into `Upload.create_for` with whatever bytes are on disk (still oversized, or truncated to 0 by a failed in-place `convert` on the same source/destination path, which then satisfies `tempfile.size > max` == false and exits the loop as "success"); the resize step cannot report "did not converge" vs "converged" vs "destroyed input" to the caller. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-67 — CPU-heavy synchronous ImageMagick + full ImageOptim pass runs up to 5 times per upload inside `create_upload`, i.e. in the request for API `synchronous` and in the single-threaded `Scheduler::Defer` queue of the web worker for everyone else, with no timeout and no concurrency bound, while the very next lines already push image work to Sidekiq (`Jobs.enqueue(:create_thumbnails...)`); one 10 MB PNG stalls every other deferred upload in that process. (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — Ruby has no overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 silently replaces the 4-dimension `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined at line 145, leaving that method dead and turning every existing 5-argument caller (e.g. width/height downsizing in Upload.create_for / avatar code) into `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` at runtime; the diff neither removes the dead definition nor audits callers (P1, conf 100)

spec/ — The diff contains zero spec changes: no controller spec exercising the new downsize loop (over-limit image shrunk, under-limit image untouched, max_image_size_kb=0 bypass, loop exhaustion), no model spec for the changed `downsize`/`optimize` signatures, and no JS test for the hard-coded 10MB client cap, so none of the new behaviour is verified (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` returns false when `convert` fails or ImageMagick is absent, but the return value is discarded and the `while` loop re-runs the identical failing command five times, then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the still-too-large file; there is no break, no log, and no user-facing message distinguishing "could not shrink" from "too large" (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — After `attempt` reaches 0 the loop exits with `tempfile.size` still above `max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` anyway, relying entirely on an unstated downstream size validation to reject the file; the requirement "automatically reduce to allowed size" has no defined outcome for the exhaustion case (P1, conf 90)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for BOTH `image` and `attachment` types, but only images are downsized server-side; a 9MB PDF now passes the client check, is fully uploaded, and is then rejected by the unchanged server-side `max_attachment_size_kb` limit, regressing the early client-side rejection for attachments (P1, conf 90)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The 10MB client cap is hard-coded and ignores `max_image_size_kb`; an admin who raises `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 will have the client reject files the server would accept, and the `file_too_large` alert reports "10240 KB" while the server-side rejection message still reports `max_image_size_kb`, giving users two contradictory limits with no site setting to reconcile them (P2, conf 90)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now unconditionally tells the user the limit is 10MB, but a 413 comes from the web server's `client_max_body_size`, which is unrelated to this constant; previously it at least reported the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb`, so the message is now wrong whenever nginx is configured differently (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:137 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, `.gif` uploads route to `resize_instructions_animated` which emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`; gifsicle's `--resize-fit` requires pixel `WxH` geometry and does not accept percentages (scaling is `--scale`), so every one of the 5 attempts exits non-zero and animated GIFs over the limit are never shrunk (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` off (the default), an over-limit animated GIF is passed through `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame, so the user's animation is silently flattened into a still image and stored as the original upload with no warning; the feature has no defined behaviour for animated originals (P2, conf 90)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `allow_animated_thumbnails` is a thumbnail-generation flag but is repurposed here to decide whether the ORIGINAL upload keeps its animation; no sibling setting (e.g. `max_image_size_kb`-style) governs original downsizing, and `authorized_extensions`/`max_attachment_size_kb` are not consulted before mutating the file (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` gates the loop, so `.svg` files (an image extension on the client `isAnImage` list) over the limit are fed to `convert ... -resize 80%` writing back to a `.svg` path, which either fails (looping 5 times) or embeds a raster in an SVG wrapper; SVG/WebP/TIFF/BMP handling is not specified or tested (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download cap is changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hard-coded `10.megabytes` regardless of `type`, so attachment URLs are now downloaded up to 10MB before being rejected by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and image URLs are capped at 10MB even when `max_image_size_kb` is configured higher (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:153 — `self.dimensions(width, height)` is deleted as a public class method with no search for external callers or specs referencing `OptimizedImage.dimensions`; the diff provides no evidence it was unused (P3, conf 50)

config/locales — ADVISORY: No locale or admin-setting description update accompanies the feature, so admins and users are not told that over-limit images are now automatically downsized (and animated GIFs possibly flattened) instead of rejected; rebuttal gate: show a `site_settings.max_image_size_kb` description or client string change (P3, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — ADVISORY: Five iterations of `-resize 80%` reduce pixel count to ~11% of the original, which for heavily-compressed JPEGs may still not reach `max_image_size_kb` and for large PNGs destroys detail without the user consenting; the shrink factor and attempt count are magic numbers with no site setting and no stated acceptance criterion for quality loss (P3, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` rewrites the upload in place and `convert_with` then runs `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)`, whose replace step renames a temp file over the path (same-device rename, new inode) while `tempfile` keeps the fd to the old unlinked inode; every later `tempfile.size` (loop guard at :66 and the `filesize` argument at :72) reports the pre-optimize size, and `Upload.create_for` computes sha1 by path but stores bytes/dimensions via the stale fd (`file.rewind` + `store_upload(file, ...)` / `FastImage.size(file)`), so the persisted Upload row's sha1 describes different bytes than the file actually written to the store and `filesize` is wrong (P1, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:129 — `downsize_instructions` emits `#{from}[0]`, and the controller selects it whenever `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, so an animated GIF over `max_image_size_kb` has its ORIGINAL upload irreversibly flattened to frame 0 before `Upload.create_for`; previously that setting only governed thumbnails and the stored original kept all frames, and nothing in the Upload row records that frames were discarded (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the downsize gate is `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` with no SVG exclusion, whereas `OptimizedImage.create_for` (:45) explicitly bypasses `convert` for `.svg`; an oversized SVG is now run through `convert big.svg[0] -resize 80%\> big.svg`, which rasterizes the vector and writes an ImageMagick-generated SVG back over the original, destroying the vector source with no record and no way to recover it (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the loop ignores `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s boolean result; when `convert`/`gifsicle` fails (non-zero exit, or `ImageOptim` raising after `convert` already truncated and rewrote `tempfile.path` via fopen "wb"), the loop spins up to 5 times on whatever bytes are now at the path and then hands them to `Upload.create_for`, so a partially written or unoptimized intermediate can be persisted as the canonical upload without any error surfacing (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` silently reclassifies existing `max_image_size_kb` data: sites whose admins already set `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 (allowed by the setting, still honored by `UploadValidator` server-side) now have uploads between 10MB and their configured limit rejected client-side, and the server-side loop turns the same setting from a hard reject ceiling into a lossy target, so identical stored values now mean different things before and after deploy with no setting migration or rename (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at :145 (Ruby: "method redefined; discarding old downsize"), so the 4-arg form is dead code and any existing caller passing `(from, to, w, h)` now binds `h` to `opts` and raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` at `!!opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` (:155), while `(from, to, w, h, opts)` raises `ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4)` (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` routes a percent geometry into `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `resize_instructions_animated` (`gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`) for any `.gif` when the setting is on; gifsicle's `--resize-fit` only parses `WxH`/`_xH` dimensions, exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, the return value is ignored, and all 5 attempts are no-ops so the oversized GIF proceeds unchanged to `Upload.create_for` (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the `while` loop discards `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s boolean; when `convert` is absent (`sh: convert: not found`, exit 127), the file is not decodable, or the SVG/ICO writer fails, the loop spins 5 times with no log or error and hands the still-oversized tempfile to `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` with no server-side guard visible in this change (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — in-place downsize on the controller's open Tempfile: `convert` truncates the same inode (fd sees new size) but `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` in `convert_with` (:164) replaces the path by rename, after which `tempfile.size` (fstat on the old inode) and every fd-based `tempfile.read` inside `Upload.create_for`/store return the pre-optimization bytes while path-based `Digest::SHA1.file` hashes the optimized inode, so the recorded sha1/filesize disagree with the stored bytes (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — ADVISORY: `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true for `.svg`, so an oversized SVG is run through `convert big.svg[0] -resize 80%\> big.svg`; ImageMagick's SVG writer emits a rasterized/traced document rather than a scaled vector (which is exactly why `create_for` special-cases `extension =~ /\.svg$/i` at :45 and copies instead); rebuttal "SVGs over max_image_size_kb are rare" does not change that the original is destroyed in place when it happens (P3, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — ADVISORY: `\`#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null\`` is a bash-only redirection; under a POSIX `/bin/sh` (dash on Debian/Ubuntu non-docker installs) it parses as `convert ... &` + `> /dev/null`, returning exit 0 immediately, and the new controller loop then re-checks `tempfile.size` before the backgrounded convert finishes and spawns up to 5 concurrent converts reading/writing the same file; rebuttal "pre-existing code" fails because the previous callers wrote to a fresh temp path once, never re-entered on the same path in a tight loop (P2, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:129 — ADVISORY: `#{from}[0]` in `downsize_instructions` selects only frame 0, so with `allow_animated_thumbnails` off an animated GIF over `max_image_size_kb` is flattened to a static image in place before `Upload.create_for` sees it; rebuttal "previously it was rejected outright" is true but the user now gets a silent content change rather than an error (P3, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for every `type` (validateUploadedFiles derives 'attachment' as well as 'image'), so the stated intent of downsizing large IMAGES silently expands to lifting the client limit on non-image attachments, which the server never downsizes: an attachment between max_attachment_size_kb and 10MB now passes the client check, uploads fully, and is rejected server-side, and the admin-configured max_attachment_size_kb no longer governs the client at all (P1, conf 100)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — the 10MB ceiling is an unstated product decision: neither docs/tasks/task-001.md ("automatically downsize large images") nor the commit message (body empty) accepts a fixed 10MB cap, yet images above 10MB are still hard-rejected client-side and never reach the new server-side downsize loop, so "large images" is quietly redefined as "images between max_image_size_kb and 10MB" without human sign-off (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:184 — `bootbox.alert(I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: maxSizeKB }))` now reports 10240 KB to the user for all upload types, but for attachments the effective limit remains the server-side max_attachment_size_kb, so the user-facing limit diverges from the limit actually enforced and admins can no longer make the message reflect their configuration (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10 MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`; a 413 comes from the web server's body-size limit which the admin sets independently, so the message now asserts a fixed 10MB that matches neither the admin's site setting nor the web server config, and the task never authorized dropping the setting from this path (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` for every API `type` (including attachments/avatars), so the server-side download cap is decoupled from the admin setting on a path the task ("downsize large images") does not cover, and non-image API downloads gain a new 10MB ceiling unrelated to max_attachment_size_kb (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — Ruby has no overloading: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at :149 silently replaces `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at :145, so the 5-arg variant the diff "kept" is dead code and any existing 5-positional-arg caller (e.g. `Upload.create_for`'s max_image_width/height in-place downsize) now raises `ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4)`; a 4-positional-arg caller binds `height` to `opts` and dies in `opts[:allow_animation]` with TypeError; inside `create_upload` there is no rescue, so in the Defer path the exception is swallowed by `Scheduler::Defer`, `MessageBus.publish` never fires and the composer spinner hangs forever with no error. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-67 — `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` re-reads `Tempfile#size`, which is `fstat` on the still-open fd, but `OptimizedImage.downsize` -> `convert_with` -> `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` replaces `to` via `rename` (same device: both in Dir.tmpdir), swapping the inode under the path; from pass 2 on `tempfile.size` is frozen at the pass-1 unoptimized size and the fd no longer points at the file on disk, so (a) the loop condition never updates and runs all 5 converts whenever pass 1 alone did not get under the limit (the normal case: 10MB * 0.64 = 6.4MB > 3MB default), (b) `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` at :72 is handed the stale oversized filesize and the validator rejects the upload as "too large" although the on-disk file is now small, and (c) when it does pass, `store.copy_file` writes `file.read` (the orphaned inode A content) while sha1 is computed from the path (inode B) — stored bytes, sha1 and filesize disagree. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — the boolean return of `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (`false` on non-zero convert exit or rescued exception) is discarded, so a failing convert (missing delegate, non-image bytes under an image extension, decode error) is re-run 5 times against the same input with zero log output (`convert_with` only logs on an exception, and `&> /dev/null` eats stderr), then execution proceeds to `Upload.create_for` as if downsizing had happened; operators have no signal that the feature is failing on their install. (P2, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `downsize_instructions` emits `convert #{from}[0] ... #{to}`; `[0]` extracts only frame 0, so any GIF over `max_image_size_kb` uploaded while `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false (the default) is silently flattened to a single still frame and stored as a successful upload — the setting named for thumbnails now decides whether the ORIGINAL upload keeps its animation, and the user gets a success response with lost data. (P2, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is true and the file is a `.gif`, `optimize` routes to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ... --output to`; gifsicle's `--resize-fit` accepts only `WxH` geometry (percent scaling is `--scale`), so it exits non-zero on "80%", the ignored `false` loops 5 times, and every oversized animated GIF is rejected as too large after 5 wasted spawns. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-67 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` matches `.svg`, and unlike `OptimizedImage.create_for` (:45 `if extension =~ /\.svg$/i` copies instead of resizing) the new loop has no SVG guard, so an SVG over the limit is fed to `convert x.svg[0] -resize 80% x.svg`, which either rasterizes it into an SVG wrapper around a base64 PNG (vector data silently destroyed, stored as success) or fails on the MSVG encoder and is rejected after 5 silent attempts. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` stops reading once the file exceeds max size and returns the truncated file rather than raising; previously such a truncated file was always > `max_image_size_kb` and rejected by the validator, but now the truncation lands at ~10MB, the loop downsizes the truncated JPEG/PNG (ImageMagick decodes premature-EOF JPEGs with exit 0) below the limit, and a corrupted image is stored as a successful API upload. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55,72 — pre-existing but now reachable with a larger window: `FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` (5s read_timeout, DNS failure, non-2xx) yields `tempfile = nil`; line 64 guards it but line 72 `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` does not, so the API caller gets a NoMethodError 500 (synchronous) or a never-published MessageBus message instead of an upload error. (P3, conf 100)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for ALL upload types (attachment, avatar, profile_background, etc.), silently discarding the admin-configured per-type limits client-side; only images are downsized server-side so this is untraceable to "downsize large images" (P1, conf 100)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now reports a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so the user-facing "file too large" message states a limit that is not tied to any configured setting or to the web server's actual body-size limit, which this change does not touch (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` raises the API URL-download cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed 10MB for every upload type (including attachments), expanding the download budget for non-image uploads, which is outside the stated intent (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — the 10MB ceiling is a magic number duplicated in three places (utilities.js:182, utilities.js:246, uploads_controller.rb:55) with no new site setting; the feature introduces an undocumented, non-configurable global upload ceiling that admins cannot see or change, which no requirement asked for (P2, conf 100)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` redefines the 4-arity `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` declared at line 145 (Ruby does not overload), so the original signature is dead and any 5-arg caller now gets `max_height` bound to `opts`; this API change plus removal of the `dimensions` helper and the `resize`/`optimize` signature churn is an unrelated refactor bundled into the feature (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` repurposes a thumbnail-generation setting to govern in-place rewriting of the original uploaded file, extending that setting's semantics beyond its name without any requirement to do so (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image? is a filename-extension check only, so a non-image (ImageTragick MVG/SVG/polyglot) payload named *.png passes and gets fed to ImageMagick `convert` synchronously in-request, yielding remote code execution. (P1, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — convert_with runs `#{instructions.join(" ")}` in a backtick shell with the tempfile path unescaped, and on the API branch that path derives from the user-controlled `type` param (Tempfile prefix "discourse-upload-#{type}") reachable now that downsize runs on upload, allowing shell command injection via metacharacters in `type`. (P1, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the downsize while-loop invokes ImageMagick up to 5 times synchronously in the request thread on attacker input up to 10MB, so a decompression-bomb or pathological image exhausts CPU/memory and blocks request workers (DoS). (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at :145 (Ruby last-definition-wins, no overloading), so the 5-positional-arg form is dead and any existing spec or caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` now raises `ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4))`, and the 4-arg form `downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` binds `200` to `opts` and dies at :155 with `TypeError` from `200[:allow_animation]` — no test in the diff exercises either the new 3-arg form or proves the old callers were migrated (P1, conf 100)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — ADVISORY: `\`#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null\`` is a bash-only redirection; under a POSIX `/bin/sh` (dash on Debian/Ubuntu non-docker installs) it parses as `convert ... &` + `> /dev/null`, returning exit 0 immediately, and the new controller loop then re-checks `tempfile.size` before the backgrounded convert finishes and spawns up to 5 concurrent converts reading/writing the same file; rebuttal "pre-existing code" fails because the previous callers wrote to a fresh temp path once, never re-entered on the same path in a tight loop (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a tight retry loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` up to 5 times based on `tempfile.size`. In `OptimizedImage.convert_with`, the command is executed via Ruby backticks using `... &> /dev/null`, which is a bash-specific redirection and is not POSIX `/bin/sh`-portable. If `/bin/sh` doesn’t support `&>`, the convert invocation may fail or behave unexpectedly, and the controller loop does not check the return value, so it will immediately re-check `tempfile.size` and re-invoke convert multiple times on the same path. This problematic interaction (retries on same file path without waiting/validating success) is introduced/exposed by the new loop even if the `&>` existed before.
